PstI is a member of a group of type II systems that are related to each other, but not closely related to any other known systems.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PstI M.R system is unique among the known type-II restriction systems in that the endonucelase is a single polypeptide, and the M and R domains are encoded on the same DNA molecule.

the M.PstIM and R.PstIM genes show no significant homology to other type-II systems, but the N-terminal domain (residues 1-206) of the R.PstIM protein shows significant sequence similarity to the R.Sau96I protein.

the N-terminal end of the endonucleases of the type-II restriction-modification system is a useful probe to search for homology in the DNA of organisms that produce PstI-like endonucleases.
